items.title: Multi-server network core
items.summary: A four-server Velocity network sharing permissions, chat and player data behind one address.
items.description: Built for a network that had outgrown a single Paper instance. Each gamemode runs isolated so a crash on minigames never touches survival, while LuckPerms contexts keep one permission tree across all of them.
highlights: Average tick time held at 12ms with 400 concurrent players
Zero-downtime restarts through rolling server cycles

items.title: Permission tree rebuild
items.summary: Ninety tangled permission groups reduced to fourteen inherited tracks in a single weekend.
items.description: The previous setup granted permissions per-user with no inheritance, so every promotion meant hand-editing forty nodes. The rebuild made rank changes a one-command operation.
highlights: Promotions dropped from 40 manual edits to one command
Documented every track for the staff handbook

items.title: Discord community architecture
items.summary: A 40-channel structure with progressive unlocks that grew a community from 400 to 12,000 members.
items.description: New members see six channels. Everything else unlocks as they verify, introduce themselves and participate — which keeps the first impression readable instead of overwhelming.
highlights: Verified onboarding cut spam joins to near zero

items.title: Closed-loop server economy
items.summary: Shops, jobs and a player market balanced so currency actually leaves the economy again.
items.description: Most server economies inflate because money enters faster than it exits. This one pairs every income source with a matching sink, and the numbers were modelled before anything went live.
highlights: Currency supply held stable across a full 90-day season

items.title: Moderation & staff systems
items.summary: Hiring rubrics, shift rotas and an escalation ladder built for an eleven-person team across three timezones.
items.description: The technical side was the easy part. The real work was writing decision rules clear enough that a new moderator on their first shift knows exactly what to do without pinging an owner at 3am.
highlights: Staff turnover fell to two departures in nine months
Every decision type mapped to a written owner

items.title: Custom quest & content chain
items.summary: Sixty custom items and a matching encounter chain that carried an SMP through its first season.
items.description: Items, mobs and quests were configured as one system, so every reward has a use and every encounter has a reason to exist beyond filling a menu.

items.title: Verification & ticket automation
items.summary: A reusable verification, ticket and logging stack deployed across eleven communities.
items.description: Built once, parameterised, then rolled out to eleven servers with different rules. Each owner received documentation for editing it without touching a bot dashboard.
highlights: Deployed across 11 communities from one documented template

items.title: Performance & stability pass
items.summary: A plugin audit and tuning pass that took average tick time from 41ms to 12ms.
items.description: Nine plugins removed, four replaced, chunk loading and entity limits retuned. No hardware upgrade required — the server was never the bottleneck.
